parts.text: Which plan is a fair test of oil temperature?

options.text: Change only the oil temperature; keep dough thickness and dropping method the same.
Keep the oil temperature constant and change the dough thickness.
Change oil temperature and dropping height together while keeping dough thickness the same.
Use the same oil temperature, dough thickness, and dropping method in both trials.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Bharti fries puris and wants to test whether oil temperature affects how the dough puffs. She can change oil temperature, dough thickness, and dropping method.

part_answers.answer: A fair test changes only the factor being tested. To test oil temperature, change that factor alone and keep dough thickness and dropping method the same.

teacher.key_rationale: Fair-test logic changes the factor under test and holds other conditions fixed. Changing thickness instead of temperature tests the wrong factor; changing temperature and drop height together is not fair; keeping every factor the same does not test temperature.
